implementation_notes: TypeScript adds no runtime, so the realization is a typed policy around the JavaScript mechanisms: cockatiel's bulkhead(limit, queue) is a promise-slot limiter that composes with timeout, retry and circuit-breaker policies through wrap(...) and rejects with BulkheadRejectedError, while generic Task<T> signatures preserve the wrapped call's type and the policy object becomes the single documented place where a dependency's capacity lives. Prefer it when several resilience policies must be coordinated; the typed p-limit variant is the lighter alternative when only slots are needed.

variants.idiom_name: cockatiel bulkhead policy composed with timeout/retry
pitfalls: Policy order changes semantics: a timeout outside the bulkhead counts queue wait, one inside does not, and a retry wrapping BulkheadRejectedError defeats the bound.
Types do not enforce capacity at runtime - generic signatures make limits look principled while the numbers still need measuring.
Keep one policy instance per dependency: sharing a single policy re-couples dependencies, and building policies per request leaks timers and listeners.
cockatiel rejects only when concurrency and queue are both full, so a large queue looks like unbounded latency.

variants.name: typed p-limit limiter
variants.implementation_notes: Minimal typed realization: wrap p-limit's limiter in a small generic module so the concurrency budget is expressed once and every dependency call is checked at compile time (await dbLimit(() => db.query<Row>(sql)) yields Row[]). Keep the limiter per dependency behind a module boundary, expose pendingCount so callers can reject fast, and add timeouts and retries as separate combinators instead of a framework; the LimitFunction type is preserved through the wrapper.
pitfalls: The generic lives on the wrapped call, not on the limiter, so a wrong type argument can make the result look narrower than it is.
The limiter is stateful and module-scoped; creating it inside a request or a test leaks queued tasks between runs.
Task errors propagate unchanged, but your own overload rejection must be excluded from retry logic or retries re-inject load.
